hints: Focus on the gas test first, relighting a glowing splint is the classic test for oxygen, so ask which Group 2 compound releases oxygen on heating.
Recall the two key decompositions: carbonates give oxide plus carbon dioxide only, while nitrates give oxide plus nitrogen dioxide plus oxygen.
To get only two different gases in total from two starting solids, both solids must release the same pair of gases, so think about what happens if both are the same type of salt.
walkthrough:
**Identify the must-have gas**

That glowing splint test tells you oxygen, $\text{O}_2$, must be one of the products. This is a big clue.

Only Group 2 nitrates release oxygen on heating. Carbonates release $\text{CO}_2$ only, chlorides and oxides do not decompose this way.

**Write the governing decomposition equations**

For any Group 2 metal M, learn these two patterns by heart.

Carbonate decomposition:
$$\text{MCO}_3 \rightarrow \text{MO} + \text{CO}_2$$
Nitrate decomposition:
$$2\text{M(NO}_3)_2 \rightarrow 2\text{MO} + 4\text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_2$$

**Count the different gases for a mixture**

The white solid is easy, $\text{MgO}$ and $\text{CaO}$ are both white, so that fits many options. The gas count is decisive.

If you mix a carbonate and a nitrate you get three different gases: $\text{CO}_2$ from the carbonate plus $\text{NO}_2$ and $\text{O}_2$ from the nitrate. If you mix two nitrates you get only two different gases in total, $\text{NO}_2$ and $\text{O}_2$, because both reactions produce the same gases.

options.A: Incorrect. $\text{CaCO}_3$ decomposes to $\text{CaO} + \text{CO}_2$, and $\text{CO}_2$ does not relight a glowing splint. $\text{MgCl}_2$ does not thermally decompose to give $\text{O}_2$, so this mixture cannot produce oxygen.
options.B: Incorrect. This is the trap. $\text{MgCO}_3$ gives $\text{MgO} + \text{CO}_2$ while $\text{Ca(NO}_3)_2$ gives $\text{CaO} + \text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_2$. That is three different gaseous products ($\text{CO}_2$, $\text{NO}_2$, $\text{O}_2$), not two.
options.C: Correct. Both $\text{Mg(NO}_3)_2$ and $\text{Ca(NO}_3)_2$ decompose by the same equation type to give a white oxide ($\text{MgO}$ and $\text{CaO}$) plus the same two gases, $\text{NO}_2$ and $\text{O}_2$. So overall there is white solid and only two gaseous products, and $\text{O}_2$ relights the splint.
options.D: Incorrect. $\text{MgO}$ and $\text{CaO}$ are already oxides and are thermally stable. They will not decompose further on heating, so no gases at all would be formed.
